domain: Religious Studies / Halakhic Theory / Commitment System Analysis
topic_summary: Analysis of the 1,900-year continuous rabbinic study of Temple sacrifice laws (Kodashim) without performance capability. The topic examines whether this constitutes living engagement with divine commandment (study-as-exercise) or preservation of obsolete practice (performance-only reading), creating a boundary case between exercising a commitment and archiving its symbol.

key_entities: Kodashim (fifth order of Mishnah/Talmud, 11 tractates on Temple sacrifice)
Second Temple (destroyed 70 CE, creating 1,900-year performance gap)
Maimonides (12th century, defended Kodashim study as equivalent to performance)
Rabbi Yohanan ben Zakkai (post-70 CE, established study/prayer/ethics as replacement)
Contemporary Orthodox yeshivot (maintain Kodashim study for messianic restoration)
Mishneh Torah vs Guide of the Perplexed (Maimonides' internal tension on sacrifice purpose)
key_tensions: Intrinsic cosmic significance vs historical concession to idolatry (Maimonidean internal contradiction)
Messianic deferral vs practical obsolescence (Orthodox preparation vs Reform abandonment)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The divine commandment structure of Temple sacrifice as encoded in Torah and elaborated in Kodashim
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Textual authority (Torah as divine revelation) interpreted through rabbinic chain of transmission (Oral Torah), with legitimacy grounded in unbroken study lineage from Sinai

readings.commitment: Studying sacrifice laws fulfills the commandment itself; the kernel remains occupied through intellectual engagement
readings.authority_grounding: Maimonidean equivalence principle ('occupying himself with the law is as if he had offered'); textual study as performative act
readings.expected_structural_delta: Zero extractiveness from performance gap; study maintains full commandment force; victim set empty (no one harmed by non-performance)

readings.commitment: Sacrifice laws are contingent on Temple existence; without altar, the commandment is suspended (husk)
readings.authority_grounding: Materialist reading of halakhic obligation; physical performance as necessary condition; Neusner's 'map without territory'
readings.expected_structural_delta: High extractiveness from continued study investment; resources diverted to obsolete practice; victim set includes those who could benefit from redirected scholarly effort

readings.commitment: Commandment is temporally suspended but not obsolete; study maintains readiness for future restoration
readings.authority_grounding: Eschatological authority (messianic prophecy); Orthodox institutional practice (Jerusalem yeshivot preparing for Third Temple)
readings.expected_structural_delta: Moderate extractiveness from opportunity cost; study justified by future contingency rather than present fulfillment; victim set includes present-generation needs subordinated to messianic preparation

axes.structural_delta: Intellectual engagement with sacrifice laws constitutes fulfillment of the commandment itself, independent of physical performance
axes.primary_observable: Institutional investment in Kodashim study (yeshiva curriculum allocation); theological defenses of study-as-substitute (Maimonides commentary frequency in responsa)
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; establishes zero-extractiveness baseline

axes.structural_delta: Physical altar performance is necessary condition for commandment fulfillment; study without performance is archival preservation, not religious obligation
axes.primary_observable: Reform/secular Jewish abandonment of Kodashim study; Neusner-style academic framing as 'fictitious territory'
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; highest extractiveness contrast with reading 1

axes.structural_delta: Commandment is temporally suspended pending messianic restoration; study maintains institutional readiness rather than fulfilling present obligation
axes.primary_observable: Third Temple preparation institutions (Jerusalem yeshivot training kohanim); messianic timeline discourse in Orthodox responsa
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; intermediate extractiveness; captures temporal dimension of kernel contest

axes.structural_delta: Yohanan ben Zakkai framework: prayer, Torah study, and loving-kindness replace sacrifice entirely, not as equivalents but as superior forms
axes.primary_observable: Liturgical substitution patterns (Hosea 14:3 'bullocks of our lips'); ethical emphasis in post-Temple rabbinic literature
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: overlaps with study_as_performance reading but focuses on replacement rather than equivalence; lower structural distinctiveness

axes.human_readable: Maimonidean Internal Tension (Guide vs Mishneh Torah)
axes.structural_delta: Maimonides' contradiction: sacrifices as anti-idolatry ruse (Guide) vs cosmic necessity requiring messianic restoration (Mishneh Torah)
axes.primary_observable: Textual analysis of Guide III:32 vs Mishneh Torah Hilkhot Beit HaBechirah; scholarly attempts at reconciliation
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: biographical/textual tension rather than structural constraint; feeds into readings but not itself a reading

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Prayer/ethics as superior replacement rather than equivalent substitute
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Overlaps with study_as_performance reading; lower structural distinctiveness; captured implicitly in reading 1's zero-extractiveness claim

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Maimonides' Guide vs Mishneh Torah contradiction on sacrifice purpose
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Biographical/textual tension rather than independent structural constraint; feeds into readings 1 and 3 but not itself a reading of the kernel

omegas.description: Is Kodashim study a D1 (functioning commitment system with interpretive drift absorption) or D4 (absent revision with covert drift accumulation)? The 1,900-year performance gap makes this genuinely undecidable: study-as-performance reading treats it as D1 (study IS the performance, no drift); performance-only reading treats it as D4 (drift accumulates covertly as 'archival preservation' masks obsolescence).
omegas.source: User's kernel contest framing + §1.3 commitment system recognition

omegas.description: Why is there no Palestinian Talmud on Kodashim despite its compilation in the Land of Israel? Does this absence signal early recognition of performance-only reading (closer to Temple destruction, less investment in obsolete study), or merely resource constraints?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + research context

omegas.description: Does contemporary Third Temple activism (Temple Institute, red heifer breeding) shift messianic_deferral from tangled_rope to snare? If restoration becomes politically feasible rather than eschatologically deferred, extractiveness increases (geopolitical risk, Palestinian displacement).
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + messianic_deferral reading

omegas.description: Neusner's 'map without territory' framing assumes performance-only reading. But if study-as-performance reading is correct, the map IS the territory (intellectual engagement constitutes the commanded act). The academic framing may itself be extractive if it delegitimizes living practice.
omegas.source: Research context + performance_only reading structural delta
